title: As-Sabur, the Patient
hookLine: the Patient, the last of the traditional list, who waits for us

lines: THE MOST PATIENT PERSON YOU KNOW.
THE LAST ONE ON THE LIST.
cards: Think of the most patient person you've ever known. A teacher who explained the same thing five times without a sigh. A grandparent who let you help in the kitchen when you were four and useless.

A friend who waited years for you to come around, and never once said, finally. Patience like that is rare, and you remember it for life. For twenty-five days, this path has walked through the most beautiful names of God.
The best-known list of ninety-nine, in the collection of at-Tirmidhi, ends with a name that's easy to miss at the bottom of the page. A good one to end on. Today: As-Sabur.

teach.b: As-Sabur comes from sabr, patience and steadfastness. Its root means to hold back, to bind, to keep yourself steady.
For people, sabr is hard work: holding on through grief, holding back from the easy wrong, holding steady when nothing changes.

The Qur'an says it often, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah is with the steadfast." But what does it mean for God to be sabur? Scholars say he sees what people do, has every power to answer at once, and doesn't hurry.
He gives time. It's close to al-Halim, the Forbearing, from a few days ago; scholars draw a fine line between them, but both say the same warm thing.

teach.h: NO ONE MORE PATIENT THAN GOD.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ put it in a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari: no one is more patient with hurtful words than God. People say the worst things about him, and still he gives them health, and still he feeds them.
So many Muslims hear As-Sabur as the God who waits: for the person who keeps promising to come back to prayer, and for the one who wandered off years ago. Look back at the whole part.

Twenty-five days: Allah, the name itself, then ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim, the King, the Holy, Peace, the Maker, the Forgiving, the Provider, the Opener, the Knower, the Hearing and Seeing, the Gentle, the Forbearing, the Loving, the Appreciative, the Trustee, the Living, the Light.
And at the end of the list, the Patient, still waiting.

how: The names are often recited as a whole list, sometimes sung, and many Muslims memorize the ninety-nine, ending with as-Sabur; patience, sabr, is praised throughout the Qur'an as a quality believers work to build.

o: the One who waits, and keeps giving health and food
the One who delays help until we've suffered enough
the One who never notices what people say

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: to hold back, to hold steady
the last name on the traditional list
no one more patient with them than God

s: the list of ninety-nine names most people know comes from at-Tirmidhi
the best-known list is in his collection, and it ends with as-Sabur.
God's patience means he doesn't see what people do
he sees, holds every power, and chooses to give time.
the Qur'an says Allah is with the steadfast

games.q: people say the worst things about God. he has all the power in the world. what does the hadith say he does?
o: keeps giving them health and food.
games.why: no one is more patient with hurtful words than God: he keeps giving them health and provision.

practice: Let one thing come to mind that you're frustrated with yourself about, the habit you keep breaking or the thing you still haven't done, and notice the voice that says, what's wrong with you.
Now talk to yourself the way that most patient person talked to you: slower, kinder, not letting you off, just not in a hurry. If you pray, you can call on God as ya Sabur.

wordCard.voice: As-Sabur. The Patient: the One who sees, holds all power, and still waits. The last name on the traditional list. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Patient. from sabr, to hold back, to hold steady.

carryVoice: Your line: he waits for you. Tomorrow the names end, and the story picks up in Medina, where the Prophet has just arrived. See you there.
